posts.content:
For most small businesses, figuring out where AI can be useful is just one more job alongside everything else they’re juggling.

Last week, I partnered with Notion to make space for that conversation. We hosted a coffee cupping with a small group of owners + operators from San Francisco’s coffee industry.

The spectrum was pretty wide -- a couple roasters had already built complex workflows for their businesses, while other operators were just getting started. We spent time discussing real workflows + challenges around inventory, taxes, logistics and quality control.

We built one of these workflows live with Mitchell from Coffee Movement, using Notion AI to turn their inventory data into a weekly delivery list.

This is the first in a series of conversations we’re hoping to have with small-business owners about how technology can support their work.

If you run a small business and there’s a workflow you wish took less time, we’d love to hear about it!

posts.content:
Over the last 6 months I've had the privilege of being able to take what I've been calling a "creative sabbatical" -- to explore a number of creative pursuits I'd given up when choosing the fast-paced startup life 10 years ago (since startup life means your work = your nights & weekends 🙂)

Since then, I've spent 3 months in Seoul, enrolled in music school, learned how to produce music, and have now begun a YouTube channel :)

The more I've dug into my creative pursuits, the more I've realized why I've been drawn to creatives and startups all along -- it's immensely powerful to be around people who have the agency to build and create the change they wish to see in this world.

Building a startup is an incredibly creative act, and becoming an artist/creative is an incredibly entrepreneurial endeavor.

Having returned to San Francisco in January, I'm excited to sit at this intersection. It's been energizing to reconnect with my friends here building ambitious companies, and to be back home to focus on my own deep work.

I'm still exploring what's next for me, but for now, I'm opening myself back up to consulting opportunities to get to know more teams out here. Whether that's running Design Sprints to help your team launch your MVP or in a "fractional founding designer" capacity, where I can help provide counsel on vetting agencies, hiring, strategy etc.

I'll leave you with my first YouTube video which I recently published. It seems to have resonated with friends who are creatives as well as those working in startups :) 

I hope this serves as an encouragement to you, and here's to creating work we'll be proud of this year ✨

Here are the 4 rules I use to get better outputs from AI:
1. Context is your superpower
2. Break big tasks into steps
3. Define what “good” looks like
4. Refine, assess & iterate

Pro tip: Star your chats by topic (health, finance, work) AI remembers everything in that chat so you can preserve context!

All of these tips work with ANY AI tool: ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity etc. free or paid
